NOT A BUG, on a corrected mechanism. Two agents independently failed to make it bite; the reviewer's job was to falsify that, and it partly did, so the reasoning here is the reviewer's rather than the implementer's.

The implementer's mechanism was WRONG: it claimed the bar is a row of fixed-px controls whose width never changes, and the reviewer disproved that by measuring the host growing 480 to 486.03px in plain English at '999 of 999', and the notice height moving 46.594 to 31.188 after measurement with no resize at all under a plausible translation.

The conclusion still holds, for a better reason. The notice is measured at its single call site in the build branch, where the count element is empty and on its 58px floor and the bar is therefore at its narrowest. That is the notice's tallest. The host width only grows afterwards, so the notice can only unwrap, so the cached value is always an UPPER bound: the cap over-subtracts and can never under-subtract. Confirmed even inside the reviewer's own falsifying run, where the cap read 90.59 against a true chrome of 75.19 and the panel still sat at 797 of an 800px viewport.

Attacks that came up empty: resizes from 1280 to 150 wide and 800 to 200 tall after measurement, chips, device pixel ratios 1 / 1.25 / 2, webfonts (there are none, all system stacks), and mutating the notice text after mount (it is set once). The bead's stated trigger, a longer translation, is currently unreachable: there is no _locales directory and no chrome.i18n.getMessage call, so the dict is hardcoded English.

Note the bead's own premise was also wrong: the English notice already ships wrapped to two lines at the natural host width. The invariant this now rests on is undocumented and untested, and that is filed as a follow-up.
